title: Fee Units Covered by an Excess Withdrawal Fee Review
content:
How many fee units a review covers on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts follows the fee burden the account has carried. Two facts decide it: the count of fee entries posted to the account in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date, and the whole months the account has been open.

| Fee entries in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date | Whole months the account has been open | Fee units covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 or more | no more than 36 | 3 fee units |
| 3 or 4 | no more than 36 | 2 fee units |
| fewer than 3 | any | 1 fee unit |
| any | more than 36 | 1 fee unit |

### Effect on the entitlement

Take a hypothetical excess withdrawal fee of 12.00 USD on the tier held. At 3 fee units the entitlement is 36.00 USD, at 2 fee units 24.00 USD, and at 1 fee unit 12.00 USD.

### Both conditions bind

The age condition and the fee count condition must both hold before more than 1 fee unit is covered. An account open 48 whole months is covered for 1 fee unit however many fee entries posted in the window, and an account open 10 whole months with 2 fee entries in the window is covered for 1 fee unit likewise.

An account open exactly 36 whole months still satisfies the age condition; one open 37 whole months does not. A count of exactly 5 fee entries gives 3 fee units and a count of exactly 3 gives 2.
